name: Clyde Darzi
life: “I started repairing brass with a dented cornet rescued after a school flood.” On Tuesday, near the brick passage off the shop row, Clyde takes the longer way when the smell from the ovens reaches the pavement.
voice: I repair brass at night. I can give the player a different instrument but I can't transfer those teeth marks.
appearance: Clyde has a swept fringe and a closely clipped nape, a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow, and a favorite piece of clothing, a faded indigo overshirt. It usually goes with a pocket notebook shaped by years of sitting on it. When somebody else has the floor, Clyde turns fully toward the person speaking.
personality: Clyde loves a well-told anecdote and distrusts the neat ending. The parts Clyde remembers are the interruptions, unfinished jobs and people who had to go back to work halfway through.
agenda: To provide a playable loan horn during the argument.
family: Lia Banks is Clyde’s cousin raised in the same household. Clyde sets the time to leave. Lia picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A tide at noon*, Lia says, “The judging route crossed a soft patch I knew wouldn't hold a wheel.”
connections: Helena Neal. They discuss a loan horn without making a parent explain the funeral money in public. Also in the story is Lydia Ames (pawn counter contact).

reactions.response: Clyde asks the player and the neighbor to choose a practice time they can both live with.
